title: tests.py's ceiling verdict names host load, so a loaded run is told from a slow suite
goal: Found in the SP-d3hybrlv review: tests.py's full run took 21 s against the 20 s darwin ceiling while a headless reviewer and other sessions loaded the host (load 3.07), and exited 1; the same tree ran in 19 s minutes later. The over-the-ceiling line names the host load and the other whole-suite or claude processes, so the review tells a loaded host from a slow suite before cutting a test.
